name: Nazi-Maoism
summary: Nazi-Maoism is a small Italian, then European, current of the late 1960s and 1970s that tried to fuse far-right racial and elitist ideas with Maoist people's war and an anti-bourgeois, anti-Western stance. Its theorist Franco Freda sought a 'fascist dictatorship of the proletariat' that would destroy the bourgeois liberal system, abolish private property, and rebuild a totalitarian, hierarchical state under a philosopher-elite.
scope: Nazi-Maoism as the defining sources describe it: the Italian far-right current of 1968-73 centred on the Rome student group Lotta di Popolo, named 'Nazi-Maoist' by the press, and on Franco Freda's writings (La Disintegrazione del Sistema, 1969, and the Gruppo di Ar manifesto), which fused Nazi racial doctrine and anti-modernity with admiration for Mao's China, anti-capitalism and a hierarchical, Platonic-Evolian state (Castriota 2023). Terza Posizione is treated by that source as a neighbouring current, not part of the scope. Excludes the French and other foreign sister groups (known only through Wikipedia), later Eurasianist and Azov-linked revivals, and Strasserism and National Bolshevism. Evidence is thin, so many answers are inferences.

sources.usedFor: Account of Freda as 'Nazi-Maoist', with quotations on democracy, parties, property, the bourgeoisie and the state. A blog quoting the primary text; quotations not checked against the Italian.

sources.title: “The Disintegration of the System”: The Nazi-Fascist Terrorism of Franco G. Freda Between Fascist Mysticism and Meta-politics During the Strategy of Tension (1969-1979), PhD thesis, full text (University of Northampton, 2023)
sources.author: Anna Castriota, University of Northampton
sources.usedFor: Scholarly definition of Nazi-Maoism (Lotta di Popolo, 1968-73), Freda's Platonic/Evolian hierarchical state, anti-capitalism, praise of Mao's China.

sources.title: The Disintegration of the System (Freda, 1969; English translation of excerpts, Hyperborea Substack copy, attributed there to 'Giorgio Freda'; not checked against the Italian)
sources.author: Franco Freda
sources.usedFor: Freda's own text: the analysis of the system, the bourgeoisie, and the proposed state.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Freda replaces the army and police with a Popular Militia of volunteers, so the armed forces are replaced, not abolished.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state-run economy would keep central control of money; the free-market premise of abolition is rejected.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The programme abolishes private property but proposes forced labor and state enterprises, not a wageless society; no statement about money was found.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Private ownership of homes is not their aim; they would eliminate private property, so ownership by every family is contrary.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Small and large landowners are dissolved into agricultural combines; all material wealth is state property.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Freda says he sought to overcome the fences of right-left and fascism-anti-fascism; the thesis calls the contraposition bourgeois.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Freda urges a lucid 'political soldier' minority to accelerate the system's fall by drastic means; the thesis describes his call to armed struggle.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Freda holds the Latin American guerrilla, the Vietnamese and the Palestinian fighter close to his outlook.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Freda sought to destroy the parliamentary liberal system and replace it with a totalitarian elite state, so parliamentary approval of spending is rejected.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Freda aimed to destroy the bourgeois liberal system through people's war, on the premise that it cannot be reformed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A state owning all wealth would control money, and independence from the government is a liberal principle.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Freda says an idea cannot be new, that principles are not verified by agreement, and praises Tradition.

character-from-environment.rationale: Freda holds that adherence to the true state comes from a priori affinities 'we dare to say are transcendental', to be discovered, not created, and says race is blood.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Freda's state would own all material wealth, leaving no role for private charity.

civilizational-union.rationale: In 1969 Freda calls for a 'supernational organic political unity' of the best Europeans while dropping the label 'Europe'; later he looks to a Europe from Siberia to Calabria. Conflicting wording, hence low.

class-collaboration.rationale: The group wanted destruction of the bourgeoisie, the worst evil in Italy, not partnership with employers.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Freda says 'class is only a bourgeois category' and that bourgeoisie and proletariat are two products of one process; he wants a new humanity in power, not a class, though he fights the bourgeoisie.

collective-farming.rationale: Freda proposed agricultural combines run by commissars, as the Fascio post notes, resembling Soviet collectivization.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The proposed state is hierarchical and totalitarian, run by an elite, which excludes confederal local assemblies.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Freda rejects parties and electoral democracy in favour of rule by a philosopher elite, which gives consent no role in legitimacy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: They rejected democracy and elections as irreformable.

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: A single Popular Judge replaces today's magistracy.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Freda attacks the bourgeois system for keeping workers docile with fridges, cars and ever new wants; the Popular State puts a consumption programme ahead of production.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Popular State is centralised: combines and enterprises feed regional presidia and a national Presidium and Regent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Freda called race 'blood, nerve' and the multiracial society a heap of 'ethnic debris'; he rejected egalitarian remedies and avowed fidelity to his own race.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Freda treats culture as an expression of racial form, and calls the Europe he wants only a certain 'superior dimension of civilization' held by some men.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: Freda holds that bourgeois democracy is a plutocratic oligarchy and parties build oligarchic groups.

democracy-best.rationale: Freda's manifesto: 'We are antidemocratic: above the fetishes of capitalist and Bolshevik democracy.'

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Freda's Gruppo di Ar manifesto states 'We are antidemocratic' and 'We are against political parties', rejecting competitive elections as the mark of legitimacy.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Freda explicitly refuses the 'foundation of the proletarian state' and class rule as the goal; he adopts communist economic measures only as an instrument and wants a hierarchical elite state.

direct-action.rationale: Freda tells followers to abandon legalistic tactics and reformist illusions and to use 'all those drastic and definitive means' to disintegrate the system; he calls electoral politics a hamster wheel.

direct-votes.rationale: Electoral politics was seen as irreformable and the group rejected democratic procedures; a 'people's state' is not plebiscitary in documents found.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Freda held that race is blood and that hierarchy is natural, and the Gruppo di Ar manifesto is against egalitarianism, so he would reject anti-discrimination remedies based on equal outcomes.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Freda calls for abolishing private property and state ownership of material wealth, so a fortune is not made fair by how it was acquired.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Freda calls the multiracial society the 'heap of ethnic debris' a group becomes when it denatures its racial form.

dominated-front.rationale: Freda's Popular State is to ally with all 'authentically anti-capitalist states' and refuse the imperialist blocs; he praises Latin American guerrillas and North Vietnam against the USA-led order.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Freda said the true state is not a simple structure of positive rights; duty and the organic state come first.

economic-freedom.rationale: State ownership of all material wealth and rejection of capitalism deny economic freedom as a condition of political freedom.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Freda said purity justifies any hardness and any deceit and the state is absolute; legal protections are bourgeois.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Their elitist, disciplined ethic of hardness and conformity to the organic state opposes eccentric individualism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Freda would leave the Atlantic Pact but have the Popular State make alliances with all anti-capitalist states, so he is not for staying out of alliances.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Freda rejected liberal democracy and bourgeois legal guarantees in favour of a hierarchical state under a philosopher-elite.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Freda opposed egalitarianism, favored hierarchical elites and racialist ideas, and wanted a Spartan, elitist society.

equal-outcomes.rationale: A hierarchical, elitist state is not egalitarian, though material wealth is to be collectively held; Freda opposed Christianity for egalitarianism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Freda calls each culture the expression of a group's 'radical racial and ethnic feeling' and the multiracial society 'ethnic debris', so a people should keep its own form.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Freda rejects liberal checks on power altogether and wants an absolute organic state, so neither exit nor the vote is valued as a check.

experts-over-public.rationale: Freda wanted a philosopher-ruler elite chosen for moral and spiritual qualities; this is rule by a qualified few rather than technocratic expertise.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: The Popular State and its Militia are to favour and collaborate with anti-capitalist movements abroad.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: All material wealth is to be state property, so foreign buyers would have nothing to buy; no rule on foreign takeovers is stated.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Freda's state is totalitarian, hierarchical and owns all material wealth, leaving no room for pluralism about economic systems.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Freda detests the Europe of trade and the market economy; exchange with foreigners is subordinated to the state's consumption programme.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican liberty theory is a liberal framework that the group did not engage; a hierarchical totalitarian state denies it.

freedom-is-self-government-of-desire.rationale: Freda says true freedom is internal discipline and respect for one's hierarchical place, not freedom toward utility.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A totalitarian state would not leave private owners free; Freda sought to abolish private property and impose state-set order.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Freda calls the multiracial society a heap of ethnic debris.

gradual-change.rationale: Freda calls for the 'subversion' of everything political that exists, accelerating its collapse, and says nothing built within the bourgeois system would last; correctives and reformist illusions are rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: Freda's organic state directs every area of life, which is the opposite of limiting the state to preventing harm to others.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Freda called for abolishing private property and state ownership of all material wealth, which leaves no room for first-claim ownership.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Freda holds that modern society descends from the decomposition of the organic state of the ancient world, whose rich and poor recognized human dignity.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: Freda's National Front fought immigration from Third World countries and holds that mixing denatures a people's form.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Private ownership of production is eliminated; income from ownership could not exist.

independent-unions.rationale: Freda's model is a totalitarian state; independent organisations of any kind would be incompatible with the proposed dictatorship.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Freda called for abolishing private property and state ownership of all material wealth, which leaves no room for private pension accounts.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Freda denied the state is a structure of positive rights, and adopted an organic, collective view.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: Freda calls for violence to destroy the bourgeois system, not just self-defence.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Freda says 'we only have accounts to settle with the Jewish or Judaized Europe' and that whoever fights Judaism must fight Zionism; he holds the Palestinian terrorist closer to his dreams.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Private ownership of capital is eliminated and a consumption programme directs production.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Freda says it was necessary 'to overcome the ideological fences right-left, fascism-anti-fascism' and wanted to overcome the right-left categories wanted by the system.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The Popular State places the individual within productive units and punishes crimes with forced labour.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Freda demanded that all material wealth belong to the state and that the bourgeois capitalist order be destroyed, so market allocation is rejected outright.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Freda asks whether it is better to save enemies of the people or 'those who die for the community'; no statement on honouring martyrs.

means-match-ends.rationale: Freda said purity justifies any hardness and any deceit, and proposed false-flag operations, so means need not mirror ends.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: The Militia's external tasks include defence and collaboration with anti-capitalist struggle abroad.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: Freda tells members to practise a radical style of militia, a 'military education of the soul'.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Freda speaks of a 'Jewish or Judaized Europe' and a 'Judaization' of Europe by America, and links usury and money to 'Jewishness'.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule by the philosopher-elite is not a mix with popular power; Plato's influence points to elite rule instead.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: The State Bank coins money whose purchasing power is guaranteed by the state's economic wealth.

more-religion-public.rationale: Freda wants a sacral state that rests on the sacred and divine, and called Khomeini's sacral society the only true revolution.

multipolar-world.rationale: Freda is against the Anglo-American order and praises Russia and an anti-Atlantic horizon; the sources do not say 'multipolar'.

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: Private enterprise is extinguished; all production is by state-organised enterprises.

municipal-property.rationale: All material wealth is to be state property.

national-rebirth.rationale: Freda wants a heroic reconquest and a 'new humanity' against a decadent bourgeois, Judaized order, but his unit is Tradition, race or Europe rather than the nation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Freda's true state is led by an aristocratic, spiritual elite of the kind Plato and Evola described, a 'natural right of heroic races', and he says a superior caste will hold power.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Freda calls capitalist and Bolshevik democracy fetishes and says bourgeois and socialist systems rest on the same economism; he wants a different state.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Freda says purity justifies any hardness and prescribes the death penalty for grave crimes against the order.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Freda wants a totalitarian state owning all material wealth, the opposite of a state limited to defence, justice and property.

no-central-bank.rationale: Private banking is eliminated and a State Bank under a State Commissar guarantees the economy's balance.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Freda calls for the denunciation of the Atlantic Pact and its military organization and says Europe has become a USA colony 'militarily'.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A head of state standing above parties as symbol is a constitutional device; the group wanted a vanguard-led state.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Freda wanted rule by a selected philosopher elite, which excludes choosing officials by lot.

one-party-rule.rationale: Freda declared himself against political parties yet wanted a vanguard leading and administering the people, so his position is split.

open-government-data.rationale: A conspiratorial elite dictatorship that rejects liberal accountability would not publish decision records for public scrutiny.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Freda tells forces to abandon legalistic bonds and use drastic means.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Freda calls himself antidemocratic and against parties; parliamentary supremacy has no place in the Popular State.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Freda calls parliamentary politics a hamster wheel and rejects reformist illusions.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Enterprise committees of all workers name commissars, but the state decides education, births and ranks, and Freda is antidemocratic.

party-controls-media.rationale: The totalitarian state directs culture, and a vanguard party leading the people would control information; stated indirectly.

person-over-state.rationale: Freda says the true state has no 'individuals' but 'men-members of the state' and the Popular State 'doesn't recognize any individually autonomous reality'.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Freda demanded that all material wealth be state property and abolished private property in all forms, so a protected private sphere is not endorsed; personal items are never addressed.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Gruppo di Ar manifesto says present parties only build 'the pillars for the success of oligarchic groups'.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Freda says purity justifies any hardness and deceit and calls for drastic and definitive means; the thesis calls his action armed struggle.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Freda treats the state as a mediator to the divine, and the thesis notes his Evolian reading of war as a clash of light and darkness.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Freda sought a total state with abolished private property, so pollution would be a matter for state command, not private suits.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Freda wants Italy out of the EEC as a neocapitalist structure but also a supernational organic unity of the best Europeans; he rejects a union of that liberal kind.

population-transfer.rationale: Anti-Jewish rhetoric and racial outlook make it plausible, but no transfer plan was documented.

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: Freda says free science serves bourgeois civilization and justice is the code of the ideas of the dominant class.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Freda's state holds all authority and owns all wealth, which leaves no room for private courts or defence firms.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Freda is antidemocratic and anti-American, and sees American liberalism as imposed on Europe.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Freda proposed a totalitarian dictatorship ruled by an elite and rejected liberal legalism, so rule through binding standing laws is opposed.

property-franchise.rationale: Freda sought to abolish private property and destroy the bourgeois liberal system, so a property-based franchise would be directly opposed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Freda said elimination of private property in all its forms is necessary.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: Freda urges short-circuiting the nervous centres of bourgeois civilization by drastic means.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Freda held that all material wealth belongs to the state, so property is subordinate to collective ends.

proportional-representation.rationale: They rejected parties and elections as irreformable; no preference between electoral systems.

public-ownership.rationale: Freda's Disintegration of the System says material wealth must be state property and private property in all forms eliminated.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Freda's National Front fought immigration from Third World countries and he holds a racial outlook; no immigration rule is stated.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Freda says 'it is another race' that gives their actions meaning and that race is 'fidelity to one's own race'.

racial-pride.rationale: Freda defines racism as 'fidelity to one's own race, recognition of the specific form of life that marks it'.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Freda called elections and parties fetishes of the bourgeois system and wanted a hierarchical elite state, not instructed delegates.

rehabilitation.rationale: Freda proposed forced-labor penal measures and said purity justifies any hardness, pointing to punishment over rehabilitation.

restore-past-order.rationale: Freda drew on Evola's traditionalism and spoke of rebirth, yet proposed a Maoist-style revolution, so restoration and progress pull in both directions.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Freda's creed holds that purity justifies any hardness; adherents are strongly ideological and reject pragmatism.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not an aim; the programme builds a state with enterprises and collectivized farms.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Freda demands the subversion of the whole existing political system.

rich-first.rationale: Its anti-bourgeois, property-abolishing stance opposes letting some people grow rich first.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Private property is to be eliminated, so converting state housing into private ownership is opposed.

rule-by-example.rationale: Freda wanted rulers chosen for moral and spiritual quality, but also hardness and coercion, so only a partial fit.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Freda would destroy the bourgeois school system and its intellectual culture, but praises Tradition and Evolian classics; split, leaning against destroying heritage.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Selfishness is bourgeois; Freda's ethic prizes Spartan sobriety, heroism and subordination to the state.

self-ownership.rationale: Freda's state treats members as parts of productive units and directs education and births.

separate-church-state.rationale: Freda says no gap should exist between the order of values and the plan of the state, which must rest on spiritual force.

separated-powers.rationale: Freda's absolute organic state concentrates authority in one elite, leaving no place for separate checking bodies.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Freda says the 'others' are 'a different soul, another race', and holds race to be blood.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Freda rejects correctives and reformist illusions and demands the disintegration of the system.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Freda's declared task is the disintegration of the bourgeois system and demolition of its structures, then the Popular State.

social-market-economy.rationale: Freda wants private property eliminated and a state economy; he rejects the market economy and the Europe of trade.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Freda says a new class in power is not the point and that the worker is not the representative of a new class; he wants a new humanity in a hierarchical state.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Freda saw the state as an absolute, not a structure of positive rights, and hardness justified by purity.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Freda rejected the Marxist view of the state as a tool of class conflict, holding it to be an organic, eternal absolute.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State enterprises and state ownership of all material wealth entail the state directing investment.

state-harmful.rationale: Freda held the state to be an organic, totalitarian and eternal absolute, the opposite of anarchist rejection of the state.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The true state sets the direction and ordains the moments by which each person reaches his authentic goal.

strong-leader.rationale: Freda praised Mao's China for a loyalty that binds the whole national community to the Leader; his own state has a Regent of the State, so a strong head is plausible but he sets no rule on bypassing gridlock.

students-direct-own-learning.rationale: The Popular State determines what each student learns; no student may choose arbitrarily.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Popular State punishes any act against its order, with forced labour or death, and the Militia is to guard against resurgence of bourgeois tendencies.

technology-design-reflects-political-int.rationale: Freda says bourgeois science and technical applications serve bourgeois civilization.

total-state.rationale: Freda saw the state as organic, totalitarian and absolute, directing all areas of life and the economy.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Freda condemns socialist states as the same bourgeois economism as capitalism, but not fascism, which he venerates.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A totalitarian unitary state would have one law; religion was not the subject.

universal-morality.rationale: Freda holds that the 'others' differ in soul and race and that freedom is differentiated by rank.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Gruppo di Ar manifesto declares 'We are antidemocratic' and rejects political parties.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: Freda says capitalists raise wages so workers buy fridges and cars, which keeps them docile.

war-builds-character.rationale: Freda praised the warrior people of North Vietnam for their Spartan, heroic style and said purity justifies any hardness, in an Evolian warrior ethos.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Private property is to be eliminated, and the bourgeois small owner was called the worst evil in Italy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Freda attacks detachment and 'apolitea' as an alibi and demands militant action.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Freda says the goal of man is not to vegetate, and that the capitalist 'intoxicates the worker with work'.

worker-ownership.rationale: Property is to be owned by the state, not by workers collectively, in Freda's scheme of state enterprises and agricultural combines under commissars.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Freda calls the bourgeois the worst evil in Italy and wants private enterprise ended.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power is to rest with a hierarchical state and vanguard rather than with councils; Freda explicitly rejected parliaments and parties but not in favor of councils.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: Freda calls for abandoning tactics 'smothered by legalistic bonds or by reformist illusions'.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Companies pass to the state and are run by commissars, not by votes.

missingStatements.text: Europe should break free of American influence and the post-war liberal order.
missingStatements.rationale: Lutte du Peuple denounced the West and called for European Socialism, and adherents were violently anti-American.

missingStatements.text: Elections and political parties are fetishes of a failing system and should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Freda's Gruppo di Ar manifesto declares 'We are against political parties' and 'We are antidemocratic'.
missingStatements.declined: Parties and elections are rejected, but the profile answers organic-representation as split and the claim is specific to this fringe; existing anti-democratic statements (one-party-rule, direct-action) already place it.

missingStatements.text: A cultural revolution should uproot the values of the bourgeoisie.
missingStatements.rationale: Freda treated the bourgeoisie as the main enemy and called for a cultural revolution to root out its world, drawing on Maoist models.
missingStatements.declined: Maoist-specific "cultural revolution" framing; the bourgeoisie/class questions (class-struggle-history, profit-exploitation) already capture the substance and few other ideologies could take a side.

notes: Later pass 2026-11-24. Evidence base is small: Freda's 1969 'The Disintegration of the System' (English excerpt), a Substack compilation of his texts and interviews, a 2023 PhD thesis and a translated Italian commentary. Searched: Freda's programme (state, economy, family, justice, militia, foreign policy), race and Zionism, religion and sacral state, elitism and democracy, revolutionary method. Answers resting only on encyclopedia summaries were re-sourced to these or nulled; social-policy themes the texts never address are null. Strands differ: Freda's Evolian traditionalism versus the Maoist mass-line of student militants.

keyFigures.role: Theorist of the 'fascist dictatorship of the proletariat'; the figure most often labelled a Nazi-Maoist
